name: Canadian C-Spine Rule
condition: Neck injury after an accident or fall

citations.text: Stiell IG, Wells GA, Vandemheen KL, et al. The Canadian C-spine rule for radiography in alert and stable trauma patients. JAMA. 2001;286(15):1841-1848.

validated_population: Alert (fully awake and oriented), stable adults 16 and older with neck pain or injury after trauma, seen in the emergency department.
self_report_note: The rule was validated with a clinician performing the exam. "Sitting up" was originally assessed in the emergency department. Do not move your neck to test it unless every earlier answer allows it.
license_note: Published clinical decision rule; criteria are not a copyrighted instrument. Question wording is original to OLA BOT.

red_flags.question: Since the injury, is there any weakness in the arms or legs, or loss of bladder or bowel control?
red_flags.help: Answer yes if you cannot lift or grip normally, or cannot control urine or stool.

red_flags.question: Did the person pass out, or are they drowsy, drunk, or not fully alert?
red_flags.help: The rule only applies to people who are fully alert. Keep the neck still and get emergency care.

items.question: Are you 65 years or older?
items.help: Age 65 or older is a high-risk factor for neck injury.

items.question: Was it a dangerous injury? For example: a fall from 3 feet or 5 stairs or higher, a diving injury, a high-speed or rollover crash, being thrown from a vehicle, or a crash on a bicycle, motorcycle, or ATV.
items.help: Answer yes if any of these happened. A simple low-speed rear-end car collision is a no.

items.question: Is there numbness, tingling, or pins-and-needles in the arms or legs?
items.help: Answer yes for any new numbness or tingling since the injury.
items.trace_label: High risk: numbness or tingling in arms or legs

items.question: Was the injury a simple rear-end car collision? (Not pushed into traffic, not hit by a bus or large truck, not a rollover, not high speed.)
items.help: Answer no if the injury was not a car collision at all.

items.question: Have you been able to sit upright since the injury?
items.help: Answer yes if you have been able to sit up on your own.
items.trace_label: Low risk: able to sit upright

items.question: Have you been able to walk at any time since the injury?
items.help: Answer yes if you have walked on your own at any point.
items.trace_label: Low risk: walked at any time since injury

items.question: Did the neck pain start later, rather than right away at the time of injury?
items.help: Answer yes if the pain began some time after the injury (for example, hours later).
items.trace_label: Low risk: delayed onset of neck pain

items.question: Gently press on the bones down the MIDDLE of the back of your neck. Is it painful to press?
items.help: Press on the center line of the back of the neck, from the base of the skull down. Muscle soreness to the side does not count.
items.trace_label: Midline neck bone tenderness (absence is low risk)

items.question: Slowly turn your head to the left and then to the right. Can you turn it at least halfway (45°) each way? Stop if you feel sharp pain or tingling.
items.help: Only do this if all earlier answers allowed it. Turn slowly and stop if it hurts sharply.
items.trace_label: Able to rotate neck 45° left and right

scoring.threshold_text: Step 1: any high-risk factor → imaging. Step 2: no low-risk factor → imaging. Step 3: unable to turn neck 45° both ways → imaging. Otherwise no imaging.

steps.label: Any high-risk factor (age 65+, dangerous mechanism, numbness/tingling)
Unable to turn neck 45° left and right

imaging.label: Neck imaging recommended
imaging.interpretation: Your answers do not allow neck injury to be ruled out by the Canadian C-Spine Rule. A neck bone injury needs to be excluded with imaging.
imaging.recommendation: Keep your neck as still as possible and get neck imaging in an emergency department.

care.where_detail: Hospital emergency department. After a high-speed crash or fall, call 911 rather than driving.
ed_redirect: Any weakness, numbness, or loss of bladder control: call 911
Severe pain when moving the neck: keep still and call 911

no_imaging.label: Neck imaging not needed
no_imaging.interpretation: The Canadian C-Spine Rule says imaging is not needed. In the original study, the rule identified all important neck injuries (sensitivity 100%).
no_imaging.recommendation: Treat neck strain at home. Get an exam if pain is not improving.

care.within: Manage at home; see primary care within 1 week if not improving
care.where_detail: Home care. Book a primary care visit if pain is not improving within 1 week.
ed_redirect: New numbness, tingling, or weakness in arms or legs
Loss of bladder or bowel control
self_care: Heat or ice for 15 minutes at a time.
